user.name: Jackson Stark
user.welcomeTitle: Jackson's back, and joining a team!
user.backstory: Charley's weather app is getting popular, and Jackson wants to help by adding a 5-day forecast. Charley invited Jackson to the project on GitHub. Time to work together.

cards.title: How teams share one project
body: A team shares one repo on GitHub. Each person works on their own branch, and changes reach `main` through pull requests, just like Charley did in the last lesson. Charley added Jackson as a collaborator in the repo's settings, so Jackson is allowed to push to it.

cards.title: Get your own copy with `git clone`
body: `git clone <url>` downloads the whole project, with its full history, into a new folder on your laptop. You only clone once. Copy the URL from GitHub, like Lily did in Unit 1.
Then move into the new folder with `cd weather-app`, and make your own branch, just like in Lesson 1.

cards.title: Review before you merge
body: When a teammate opens a pull request, you review it on GitHub. Read the changes in the Files changed tab, leave comments, then choose Approve or Request changes. Reviews catch bugs before they reach `main`.

cards.title: Stay up to date
body: Your teammates keep merging things into `main`. Before you start something new, switch to `main` and run `git pull`, so you're building on the latest version and not an old one.

questions.prompt: Download Charley's project to Jackson's laptop. Use the Copy button on the profile card.
You're in the project folder. Create a branch called `add-forecast` and switch to it.
Jackson finished the forecast and opened a pull request. While reviewing it, Charley spots a bug. What should Charley do?
options: Leave a review and choose "Request changes"
Merge it anyway and fix the bug later
questions.wrongFeedback: That's what reviews are for: Charley chooses "Request changes" so Jackson can fix the bug before it reaches `main`.

questions.prompt: Jackson fixed the bug, and Charley merged the pull request. Why should Jackson run `git pull` on `main` before starting something new?
options: To upload Jackson's work to GitHub
To get everything the team merged, so new work starts from the latest version
questions.wrongFeedback: `git pull` downloads what teammates merged, so Jackson builds on the newest `main`. Uploading is `git push`.
